deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page is a draft of the part of Riemann's Inaugural-Dissertation (1851, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse') that follows the integral theorem (Art. 7-9) and the regularity theorem for solutions of Laplace's equation (end of Art. 10). The previous page set up the general principle. If dX/dx + dY/dy = 0 in a simply connected surface T, then the boundary integral of (X dy/ds - Y dx/ds) over every piece of T vanishes. Hence the integral from a fixed O_0 to a variable O is path independent and defines a function of (x,y). The next page gives the maximum principle and the identity theorem for harmonic u (dissertation Art. 11, Sätze I-III).

First paragraph. The surface T, traced out by the point O, is assumed simply connected 'as before' and spread out over the plane A only simply (a single sheet, no branch points).

Main argument. A complex quantity w = u + v i is given on T under hypotheses numbered 1-4. From the use made of them, these are (my reconstruction):
- (1) du/dx = dv/dy;
- (2) du/dy = -dv/dx;
- (3), (4) finiteness/continuity conditions allowing exceptional points or lines.

Step 1. By 2, 3, 4 and Art. 9 (Green/Gauss integral theorem; 'III = 0'), the boundary integral vanishes for every part of T:
  ∮ (u dx/ds - v dy/ds) ds = 0.
Check (mine): by Green, ∮(P dx + Q dy) = ∬(Q_x - P_y) dx dy. With P = u, Q = -v this gives ∬(-v_x - u_y) = 0 by (2). In the form of the previous page, take X = -v, Y = -u; then X_x + Y_y = -(v_x + u_y) = 0.

Step 2. Hence U(x,y) := ∫_{O_0}^{O} (u dx/ds - v dy/ds) ds has the same value along every path from O_0 to O in T. With O_0 fixed, U is a continuous function of (x,y), and its differential is dU = u dx - v dy. So
  dU/dx = u, dU/dy = -v.

Step 3. Substitute u = U_x and v = -U_y into hypothesis 1: U_xx = -(U_y)_y, i.e. U_xx + U_yy = 0. Hypotheses 3 and 4 become the exceptional-set conditions of the Lehrsatz at the end of Art. 10. That theorem says such a function is, together with all its derivatives, finite and continuous at all points of T.

Step 4. Therefore the same holds for w = dU/dx - i dU/dy = u + i v and for all its derivatives with respect to z. This is Riemann's proof that a complex-differentiable function with removable exceptional points is infinitely differentiable. He gets it by reducing to the regularity of harmonic functions via the harmonic conjugate/potential U.

§20 (heading uncertain, perhaps 'Ueber ... Flächen'): only abandoned beginnings survive. The aim is a rule valid in all cases for the determining conditions on the given quantities, and for the range ('Umfang') of what remains arbitrary in the quantities to be determined. This is the dissertation's programme of characterising a function by boundary/discontinuity conditions and counting the free parameters. The isolated line at the bottom is an insertion: '... if somewhere in the surface a piece, i.e. a single boundary point, were assumed'. It refers to isolated points treated as boundary (exceptional) points.
errors: No mathematical errors. Riemann writes ∂x/∂s for dx/ds (a notational looseness). The hypotheses 1-4 are referenced but not restated on this page; the identification of 1 and 2 with the two Cauchy-Riemann equations is inferred from the computation and is fully consistent with it.

The path-independence claim needs simple connectivity of T after excluding the exceptional points. That is supplied by the stated assumption and by hypotheses 3-4 together with the removability argument of Art. 10.

results.what: Vanishing of the boundary integral of u dx - v dy over every subregion, given du/dy = -dv/dx (via the Green/Gauss integral theorem)
results.modern_name: Green's theorem / Cauchy integral theorem (real form)
results.usually_credited_to: Green 1828, Gauss; Cauchy 1825 for the complex version

results.what: Construction of a potential U with U_x = u, U_y = -v by path-independent integration in a simply connected domain
results.modern_name: Existence of a potential for a closed 1-form in a simply connected domain (Poincaré lemma)
results.usually_credited_to: classical (Euler/Gauss era); Riemann uses it systematically in the 1851 dissertation

results.what: A complex function satisfying the Cauchy-Riemann equations, with removable exceptional sets, has all z-derivatives finite and continuous; proved by reduction to regularity of harmonic functions
results.modern_name: Infinite differentiability of holomorphic functions / removable singularities (Riemann's theorem on removable singularities)
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy (via integral formula); Riemann 1851 dissertation, Art. 12

results.what: Programme (§20, unfinished) of determining a function by conditions and counting the remaining arbitrary quantities
results.modern_name: Riemann's characterisation of analytic functions by boundary/discontinuity data (precursor of the Riemann-Roch counting)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of Art. 12 and the opening of Art. 20 of Riemann's published 1851 dissertation. The method (a potential U plus the harmonic regularity theorem of Art. 10) is exactly the published argument, so there is nothing new beyond drafting details.

checkable.asserts: With u=U_x, v=-U_y, the CR equation u_x=v_y is equivalent to Laplace's equation U_xx+U_yy=0 (expression is 0).

checkable.asserts: The Green's-theorem integrand for ∮(u dx - v dy) is -(u_y+v_x), so it vanishes iff u_y=-v_x.

transcription_corrections: First line likely reads 'Ist die durch den Ort des Punktes O gebildete Fläche T, folglich wie vorhin einfach zusammenhängend und eine überall nur einfache Ausbreitung über die Ebene A ...'. The image shows 'gebildete' rather than 'bildende', and 'einfache Ausbreitung' rather than 'ein[?] Ausbreitung'.

'erhält daher ... erstreckt denselben Werth' should read roughly 'erhält daher, durch jede von O_0 nach O gezogene Linie erstreckt, denselben Werth, und bildet, O_0 als festgedacht, eine stetige Function U von x, y, von welcher der Differentialquotient in jedem Punkte ... dU/dx = u und dU/dy = -v ist'.
The integrand is written with ∂x/∂s and ∂y/∂s in the manuscript, i.e. dx/ds and dy/ds.
The §20 heading is uncertain in the image. 'zweiblättrige' is doubtful; the visible letters suggest 'Ueber zwei ...' or similar, and it should be marked as unread.

In the §20 fragments, 'Begriffsbestimmung'/'Begriff' are probably '(Inbegriff/Angabe) der Bedingungsgleichungen für die gegebenen Grössen' and 'die Angabe des ... für die zu bestimmenden Grössen noch willkürlich bleibenden Umfangs'.
The isolated bottom line reads approximately 'wenn irgendwo in der Fläche ein Punkt (d. h. ein einzelner Begrenzungspunkt) angenommen würde'. 'Punkt' rather than 'Stück' is probable from context.
